items.article: Trump is sending $500 checks to nearly a million Americans insured under the ACA ahead of the midterms, with a letter promoting his healthcare record. President Donald Trump is sending $500 checks to nearly a million Americans this week, along with a letter promoting his record on healthcare. The US Treasury is releasing the checks to over 950,000 Americans across 30 states who were enrolled in Affordable Care Act health insurance plans, an administration official said. The letter from the president was set to be mailed out to recipients on Thursday. "For years, the Biden Administration overcharged you to fund the operation of HealthCare.gov. That money belongs to hard-working Americans, not the Government, and now, I am returning it to you!" Trump begins the letter. Trump previously announced plans to send out the Affordable Care Act refund checks in early September, saying the Biden administration had overcharged enrollees and "accumulated a significant surplus of funds that were not used to benefit the Americans who paid these higher premiums." The payments are coming about a month before Americans head to the polls for the midterm elections . They're also part of a trend of Trump promising cash payments in his second term. The president said this month he would send every American adult a $5,000 " Trump dividend " if Republicans maintained control of the House and Senate in November. items.text: Changes to SNAP benefits begin Oct. 1 for millions of Americans: What to know
items.article: Major changes are coming on Oct. 1 for the tens of millions of Americans who rely on the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) for food assistance. 5 million Americans, including over 1 million children, lost benefits this year. Major changes are coming on Oct. 1 for the tens of millions of Americans who rely on the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) for food assistance from the federal government. In the short term, most families will see a slight bump in their monthly payments to help afford groceries. But in the coming months, households will face stricter eligibility requirements and changes to how the benefits are administered that could ultimately result in far fewer benefits. An estimated five million Americans -- including more than 1 million children -- have already lost SNAP assistance over the past year as part of President Donald Trump’s signature tax and spending law, according to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities. Every year on Oct. 1, the federal government adjusts its monthly SNAP benefits to account for inflation. These cost-of-living adjustments apply across all states. For a typical single-person household in one of 48 states (not including Alaska or Hawaii), checks will go from a maximum of $298 to $306 per month. That’s an extra $8 monthly.

items.text: 'I work at Bolton Aldi during the day - but in the evening I earn £1,300 an hour'
items.article: 54-year-old dad of two, Andy Pojaysk, from Bolton's successful side-hustle means he goes on more holidays and is looking to retire early A hard-working dad is now looking towards early retirement after creating a successful side-hustle that has brought in over £230,000 in sales. Andy Pojaysk, a 54-year-old Aldi store manager from Bolton , started his business when looking to clear out his bulging wardrobe of old clothes he no longer wore. The dad-of-two's journey began one day as he was scrolling through social media when an advert caught his eye. "I think it said something like, 'You can get yourself a pair of trainers possibly for like 20 quid or something'," said Andy. "I clicked on it, and it told me to download the Tilt app, which I did. There were obviously a few sellers on, so I scrolled through, and I actually ended up buying a hoodie or something. "Then I bought a couple more bits, and then eventually on the app there was a little section that sort of said 'Would you like to become a seller?' So I was watching people do it and I just thought that's something I could probably do in my spare time to make a little extra money."

items.article: The era of the US being the most powerful and vital nation in the world is drawing to a close – thanks to Maga Welcome to Trump’s America , The i Paper ’s World Insight series presenting the sharpest, deepest thinking on an era-defining shift in history and politics, investigating how Donald Trump and his administration have changed the US and the world – and where we go from here. • $120,000 should be a great salary. In these US states, it isn’t • Brash America is facing its worst nightmare: loneliness • Maga’s worst nightmare: a child-free, unmarried female president For decades, geologists, environmentalists and energy company spokespeople have debated the concept of “ peak oil ” – that moment when the global production and consumption of oil would finally begin to decline. For the American geologist M. King Hubbert, who developed the theory in the 1950s, it was important because both supply and consumption would fall sharply after it reached its peak. We’d keep pumping the stuff at a high rate until it became clear that it was nearly gone, and then we’d have barely any time to adjust to the fact that the global tank was empty . Is it crazy to wonder if the same logic could apply to countries, as well as resources? Specifically, should we already be talking about peak America ?
